claims.text: The AWSx ELB component provides APIs for provisioning Application and Network Load Balancers and integrates with API Gateway, ECS, Lambda, and VPC.
The example AWSx load balancer listens on port 80 in the account's per-region default VPC using its public subnets, exposing it to the internet.
ALBs automatically open ingress traffic to the ports they listen on, whereas NLBs do not.
The AWS provider registry has API docs for the ec2 LaunchTemplate resource at /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/ec2/launchtemplate/.
AWSx uses the target group passed in the task definition's portMappings to populate the ECS service's load balancer configuration.
The AWSx ECS component (awsx.ecs classes) automatically creates the right ingress and egress rules; raw aws.ecs requires manual security group rule management.
The ECS Fargate nginx example exports a stack output named `url`.
ALBs offer two features that make them more attractive than NLBs for ECS: dynamic host port mapping and path-based routing with priority rules.
By default, an AWSx load balancer is created as internet-facing, using the VPC's public subnets.
The AWSx load balancer accepts a `subnets` property (subnet objects) or a `subnetIds` property (subnet IDs).
The `listener` property chooses smart defaults based on whether the listener is created against a load balancer or a target group.
NLBs support TCP, TLS, UDP, TCP_UDP, QUIC, and TCP_QUIC listener protocols, while ALBs support HTTP and HTTPS; NLBs default to TCP.
AWS docs URLs rule-action-types.html#fixed-response-actions, #redirect-actions, and listener-rules.html exist for the ELB listener rules content.
The `deregistrationDelay` range is 0–3600 seconds and the default is 300.
The `slowStart` range is 30–900 seconds or 0 to disable, and slow start is disabled by default.
Stickiness is supported for ALBs only.
Target group `targetType` values are instance, ip, lambda, and alb; the default is instance; IPs must be within VPC private range, RFC 1918 ranges, or RFC 6598 range (100.64.0.0/10).
Health check `interval` range is 5–300 seconds with a default of 30 seconds.
Health check `healthyThreshold` range is 2–10 and default is 3.
Health check `unhealthyThreshold` range is 2–10, default is 3, and for NLBs must equal healthyThreshold.
Health check `timeout` range is 2–120 seconds; AWS default is 6 seconds for HTTP target groups and 10 seconds for HTTPS, TCP, and TLS target groups.
